title: Schematic symbols (Figures T-1, T-2, T-3)
idea: Each symbol is a little drawing of the part. Learn the shape and the number on the figure won't matter.

items: Circle with a bar and an arrow
Two coils with a core between

parts.name: Transistor
parts.look: A circle with a bar inside and an arrow on one lead.
parts.job: It controls the flow of current. Here it switches the lamp on and off.

parts.name: Lamp
parts.look: The dome shape with a loop inside.

parts.name: Battery
parts.look: Long and short parallel lines, stacked.

parts.name: Single-pole single-throw switch
parts.look: One arm that opens or closes one connection: a plain on/off switch.

parts.name: Transformer
parts.look: Two coils facing each other with straight lines (the core) between them.

parts.name: Capacitor
parts.look: One straight plate and one curved plate.

parts.name: Light emitting diode
parts.look: A diode symbol with small arrows pointing away from it: light coming out.

parts.name: Variable resistor
parts.look: A zigzag with an arrow touching it.

parts.name: Variable inductor
parts.look: A coil with an arrow tapping into it.

compare.how: Two coils with a core between them.

traps.why: The lamp is component 3, the dome. Component 2, the circle with a bar and arrow, is the transistor.
Ground is the short slanted lines at the bottom. Long and short parallel lines are a battery.
An inductor is drawn as a coil. A zigzag with an arrow is a variable resistor.
There's no arrow, and there are two coils with a core between them: a transformer.
The variable capacitors are the plates with a slanted arrow (component 2). Component 3 is a coil: a variable inductor.

traps.wrong: Give off light when current flows through it
traps.why: That's the lamp's job. The transistor controls the flow of current that lights it.
